Electric first Electric first. Fast followed. I came to motorcycles through electricity first. A commuter Zero became a Bonneville record bike, then a development platform for racing, charging, and software—and took me to Pikes Peak. Open chapter → Make hidden systems legible From artificial vision to local-first tools. My favorite technology gives people more agency: restoring a signal, exposing a hidden system, shortening the distance between an idea and a useful tool. Open chapter → Service before spectacle Build for people. Stay useful. Military service, community leadership, overseas intelligence and technology work, and mental-health advocacy all shaped the same operating principle: make the work practical, humane, and accountable. Open chapter → Practice is the through-line Japan, Zen, and the discipline of attention. Living and attending high school in Japan gave me a vocabulary of practice long before I had a vocabulary for product design, leadership, or engineering.
